So to have Brown play in a corner of the NPR Music offices with an 11-member group was dream come true for a lot of NPR staffers. Chuck Brown: Tiny Desk Concert May 16, 2012 4:00 PM ET By Frannie Kelley Chuck Brown Tiny Desk Concert The name Chuck Brown might not mean a whole lot to people outside the Washington, D.C., area. That would be their loss. In D.C., Brown is widely known, even revered, as the Godfather of Go-Go, a title he's held since the late '70s. Though he started out as a jazz guitarist, Brown invented go-go, a style that incorporates funk, jazz, R&B, hip-hop and dancehall, and has mostly stuck with it ever since. No one in D.C. can really explain why go-go hasn't traveled beyond the city's environs — we love it here, it's all over our commercial R&B and hip-hop radio stations and, at least when I was in high school, a go-go in a school's gym was the most packed party of the weekend. Chuck Brown is a local hero. A few days after he played our offices, Brown and his whole band played at the Redskins' stadium for the halftime show. Sponsor Message So to have Brown play a corner of our office — not a 90,000-capacity football stadium — was like a dream come true for a lot of NPR staffers. pages.text: Civil Enforcement Actions | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Civil Enforcement Actions While the vast majority of union officers and employees do their work diligently and without incident, unfortunately civil violations do sometimes occur and, when they do, the union is the victim. The Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) conducts civil investigations of alleged violations of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA) and related laws. These investigations by OLMS District Offices involve issues such as union officer elections, the filing of required reports by unions, employers, and labor relations consultants with OLMS, and the imposition of trusteeships over subordinate unions by a parent body. These investigations may result in Civil Enforcement Actions or, in election cases, Voluntary Compliance Agreements reached without resort to litigation. pages.text: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike 6 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Nick Beake , Europe correspondent, Madrid , Guy Hedgecoe , Madrid and Alba Morgade Watch: Protesters and police clash in Barcelona Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. NPS / Tahzay Jones With climate change occurring throughout the north, immense changes are happening to landscapes, wildlife, habitat, and human lifestyles in all of Alaska’s national parks. Observations from people living in and near parks on the frontlines of climate change demonstrate how deep the impacts can be. It’s not just about whether there are more or less bears in a park or that a recreational hiking trail is not accessible. Seasonal changes, unreliable ice conditions, thawing permafrost, and differences in animals and habitat all affect human activities and use of resources. This provides new insights into what climate change means for Alaska’s national parks. I can do all the science in the world up here, and I can know from the bottom of my heart that this place is critically important, but unless I can help with sharing the message of how important it is, and why people should care, and what is changing up here, it’s not going to get very far. –

NPS It’s important to understand that climate change isn’t just an academic issue for scientists and resource managers. Firsthand experiences with climate change can be dramatic, life-changing, and sometimes life-threatening for people who work, live, and travel amid such changes. Why should you care if the sea ice is changing, or winters in Alaska are warmer and wetter? Because what happens in the Arctic doesn’t stay in the Arctic. A shifting Arctic climate has global environmental, economic, and social implications. For example, the Arctic helps regulate the world’s temperature and global weather patterns, so changes in the far north can cause more storms, wildfires, drought, and flooding in lower latitudes. From anaesthesia and antiseptics, to medical imaging and new, minimally invasive techniques—each innovation has helped surgeons operate with greater confidence and precision. Nearly 150 sites across the country have been closed in the textile hubs of Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur this weekend. The garment industry is big business for Bangladesh, generating nearly $40bn (£30bn) in exports every year and making up 10% of the country's total GDP. Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month. The minimum monthly wage in Bangladesh is currently 12,500 taka but employees say this is not enough to deal with the cost of living crisis. On Sunday morning workers massed on the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur to block the road. Traffic was stopped by the protests for about an hour before police stepped in. A "No Work No Pay" provision of labour laws allows owners to suspend operations and withhold wages when production is disrupted. While I had done so in the past, way before these two months, this period turned out to be a great adventure that I’m still hiking. It was a time after Project CaCau . When I put it to an end, I felt not only disappointed, but ambitious. Why exactly? Well, I don’t know, but the roaring engine I had used to keep me going through that project was still on, and I couldn’t just stop it. So, I had to redirect it somewhere. For a bit, I had just redirected it to OSM. I experimented with multiple things and tried to pick up my old stuff. But one in particular caught my attention. A while ago, I was editing the river area of the Ilagan River. I never picked it up again until then. Despite that, it just stuck. Oh, where do I start? It was around October when I had recently imported the barangay boundaries of my hometown, Cauayan City. I had just asked the GIS team at the local Planning and Development Office to adjust the boundaries again, as many issues were identified in the dataset. A while later, I had an idea to try to help the GIS team adjust the boundaries, because I figured, “Why not?” and they’re probably doing a lot of work already, given so many developments in the area. A little back and forth, but then they stopped responding. I mean, it is basically a 50/50 chance that they respond or not. A little later, I dove into further research and stuff, and I thought of asking an institution to collaborate with me on making a dataset for the PDO to use and merge with theirs, so it can be as accurate as possible (I like things accurate). Thus, Project Cadastral Cauayan (CaCau) was born. I first emailed the Isabela State University. I chose them especially because of the Cauayan Campus. In my eyes, they were the most capable (and probably only) institution in the area to pull this off. It was February 27 of this year. No response, so I kept trying new email addresses, follow-ups, and at one point, Messenger. Too many alternatives with no response, and about two months later, nothing. Until finally, through the Cauayan Campus’ newspaper email, the Kawayan Communicator, a Messenger notification popped up.

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Community, Fire, and Enforcement Jun 8, 2026 On June 3, 2025 at approximately 2 p.m., a member of the Salmon, Idaho community reported smoke in the West Fork of Wimpey Creek on Bureau of Land Management managed lands. Central Idaho Dispatch received the call and promptly mobilized firefighting forces. A US Wildland Fire Service fire engine responded, heading up the steep, rocky road toward the location of the smoke report. A United States Department of Agriculture Forest Service (USDA FS) helicopter launched to assist and located the smoke high on the ridgeline in topography difficult to navigate by ground crews. With the helicopter holding a hover, four heli-rappellers descended by rope to the scene of the fire and were joined by other US Wildland Fire personnel. The firefighters sized up the fire at approximately one-quarter acre, 30% active, and creeping on a 20-40% slope in timber, grass, and dead/downed timber with 3-5 mph south-southwest winds. Probablemente usted se pone filtro solar y se lo pone a sus hijos cuando van a la piscina o a la playa. La protección solar es importante durante todo el año, y lo mejor es usar varios tipos diferentes. Congenital Zika Syndrome and Other Birth Defects For Everyone Oct. 26, 2026 What to know Zika virus can spread from an infected pregnant woman to her fetus. Infection during pregnancy can lead to congenital Zika syndrome and other birth defects. Zika virus infection does not impact future pregnancies. Overview of Zika-associated birth defects Zika virus infection during pregnancy can cause birth defects of the brain or eye. These birth defects can occur alone or with developmental problems in a particular pattern called congenital Zika syndrome. The following conditions can occur in a baby with congenital Zika virus infection: Smaller than expected head size, called microcephaly Problems with brain development Feeding problems, such as difficulty swallowing Hearing loss and vision problems Seizures Decreased joint movement, called contractures Stiff muscles, making it difficult to move Not all babies born with congenital Zika syndrome will have all of these conditions. Video by Nicely Done Productions By Sam Kent Last updated August 12, 2026 Cities are constantly evolving. They are built up, layer by layer, each generation leaving its mark on the one before. Roman roads became the foundation for medieval streets. Aqueducts gave way to railways, electricity, and underground transportation. Over time, every city’s infrastructure becomes a record of the people who shaped it years before. Walk through Rome, and the history is impossible to ignore. Ancient walls sit beside modern apartments; the remains of a long-gone empire lie under busy streets. Layers of the past can be felt everywhere: yet Rome, just like every great city, cannot stand still. Today, millions of visitors and residents move through the city, expecting to stay connected above and below ground. From GPS and wayfinding tools to digital tickets and tap-to-pay features for transport systems, to instant communication between families and friends. The challenge is that today’s expectations for connectivity must be woven into yesterday’s infrastructure, without damaging what lies beneath. Los sitios web seguros .gov usan HTTPS Un candado ( ) o https:// significa que usted se conectó de forma segura a un sitio web .gov. Comparta información sensible sólo en sitios web oficiales y seguros. Consejos para la búsqueda Inglés (English) Imprimir Páginas relacionadas Este documento presenta conceptos básicos de búsqueda y describe las técnicas más avanzadas que pueden ayudarle a realizar búsquedas con mayor eficacia. Para comenzar la búsqueda Ampliación de la búsqueda Operadores de búsqueda avanzada Para buscar un documento, escriba algunas palabras descriptivas en el cuadro de búsqueda y oprima la tecla Enter (Intro) o haga clic en el botón Buscar. En respuesta, Google muestra una página de resultados con una lista de documentos y páginas web relacionadas con los términos de búsqueda y ordenadas según su relevancia. De forma predeterminada, Google solo muestra páginas que incluyen todos los términos de búsqueda, por lo que si quiere ampliar o limitar la búsqueda debe añadir más términos o quitar algunos. Usted no necesita escribir "and" entre los términos de búsqueda.
